Name: Aspect of Ivsil
Source: Lyres Guide to Risk and Reward
Information: Ivsil the Feathered Storm is a living disaster who embodies storms, hurricanes, and the ferocity of the wind. It is the most destructive among the Paraprismatic gods, and part of its assigned role is to ensure errant air elementals are confined to the Elemental Plane of Air. However, if it is unleashed upon the Material Plane or encounters any creature not within its domain, it is known to act like a savage beast and wildly destroy everything within sight. Many times in history, cults have attempted to summon it into the Material Plane to bring about an age of destruction, and luckily it has never managed to remain for long. However, the times it has been conjured have all led to the destruction of civilization surrounding it.

Stat Blocks.title: Aspect of Ivsil

traits.name: Living Storm (Mythic Awakening)
traits.description: When Ivsil is reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright, its hit points are instead reset to 300, regains all spent uses of Legendary Resistance, recharges their Unleash Tempest, and can immediately move up to their movement speed without provoking opportunity attacks. For the next hour they can use their Mythic Action options. A party who defeats Ivsil after using Living Storm is awarded an additional 75,000 XP (for a total of 150,000 XP).

traits.name: Shifting Body of Wind
traits.description:
When Ivsil moves through the spaces of other creatures, it discorporates and becomes a living wind, allowing Ivsil to suffer no penalty to their movement. They must end their movement in an unoccupied space, however, or else be shunted to the nearest one when their turn ends and take 1d4 damage for every space they were shunted through/into.

Ivsil automatically succeeds in any attempt to avoid or escape a grapple or effect restraining it. If it does so, however, it must drop any objects or creatures it is grasping or grappling.

actions.description: Ivsil makes one Bite and four Claw attacks. It can also replace its Bite with a use of Grand Wingbeat.

actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +16 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 13 (2d12) lightning damage.

actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (2d12 + 8) slashing damage.

actions.name: Unleash Tempest (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Ivsil unleashes its control over the wind by using one of the following tempest options: Shredding Hurricane or Triple Vortex.

options.name: Shredding Hurricane
options.description: Ivsil surrounds itself with a huge sphere of hurricane-strength winds, lightning, and shredding currents. This sphere extends 40 feet out in each direction from Ivsil, completely obscuring itself to those outside and causing all ranged attacks made against it to have disadvantage. Creatures (apart from Ivsil) who start their turn within the sphere or enter it for the first time on their turn must make a DC 25 Strength saving throw, and on a failure they are knocked prone and take 18 (4d8) lightning damage and 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage. Once knocked prone this way their movement speed is reduced to 0 until the start of their next turn. Creatures who make concentration checks within the sphere do so with disadvantage (except Ivsil). Once used, Ivsil must concentrate on this effect as though it were a spell. It ends after 1 minute, if Ivsil loses concentration, or if Ivsil does not choose to use its action to sustain the effect at the start of each of its turns.

options.name: Triple Vortex
options.description: Ivsil chooses three points it can see within 240 feet of itself, and from each of those points a tornado appears. Each tornado fills a cylinder with a radius of 15 feet and a height of 120 feet. Every creature caught within a tornado must make a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw, being pulled 60 feet into the air and taking 28 (5d10) bludgeoning damage and 28 (5d10) force damage on a failure, or half as much damage and are not pulled into the air on a success. The tornados hold creatures that failed aloft in the air, prone, until the start of Ivsil’s next turn, at which point the tornados disappear and the creatures plummet. Creatures who attempt to right themselves from prone in the air must succeed a DC 25 Athletics check or be unable to do so, and while held prone this way their movement speed is reduced to 0. Creatures who right themselves in the air and have a fly or fly (hover) speed can move only using those speeds, and the tornado counts as difficult terrain. Ivsil is entirely unaffected by the tornados should it enter them.

actions.name: Mythic Action: Grand Wingbeat
actions.description: Each creature within 20 feet of Ivsil must make a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw, taking 20 (3d12) bludgeoning damage on a failed save.

Each creature in that cone must succeed a DC 24 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of Ivsil until the start of Ivsil’s next turn. A creature who succeeds this save becomes immune to this effect for 24 hours.

options.name: Galeforce Rage (Costs 3 Actions)
options.description: Ivsil summons wrathful meteors of wind and lightning from the sky, causing them to strike eight points Ivsil chooses within 1 mile of itself. Each meteor explodes in a 15-foot-radius sphere, forcing all creatures inside of each to make a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw. Creatures that fail take 13 (2d12) lightning damage and 7 (1d12) force damage. Structures and vehicles take twice as much damage on a failure.

options.name: Maximum Aura (Costs 2 Actions)
options.description: Ivsil surrounds itself in a veil of defensive wind until the start of its next turn, during which time it reduces all damage it takes by 10 points and its AC increases by 3.

options.name: Death Whirlwind (Costs 3 Actions)
options.description:
Ivsil chooses one creature it can see within 120 feet of itself, and causes a violent twister to appear around them, sucking away oxygen. That creature must succeed a DC 20 Constitution saving throw or it starts to suffocate, and while suffocating this way it must repeat the save at the start of each of its turns. If they succeed, the effect ends. If they fail, they continue to suffocate and are treated as if they had been suffocating for 1d4+1 additional turns. Any creature who starts their turn adjacent to the targeted creature or enters such a space for the first time on their turn also makes this Constitution saving throw, but the effect ends for them if they leave those spaces.

A creature who succeeds their saving throw against this effect cannot be targeted by it again for 1 hour.
